key_insight: Turning discrete, verifiable 3D physical checks into smooth, continuous rewards gives dense learning signals that let vision–language models learn precise numerical spatial reasoning instead of relying on sparse relative rankings.
problem_solved: VLMs struggle with accurate numeric predictions for 3D scene understanding because standard RL-style training (e.g., relative ranking) produces sparse rewards, unstable gradients, and discards informative "near‑miss" cases that carry verifiable physical signals.
method: Define verifiable physical constraints from 3D geometry/physics as ground-truth checks (e.g., distances, collisions, alignment) rather than only relative ranks.
Design a smooth verifiable reward (SVR) function that maps those discrete checks into continuous, differentiable signals to provide dense gradients while preserving verifiability.
Integrate SVR into the VLM training loop (reward shaping / RL fine-tuning) and replace or augment relative-normalization schemes to stabilize learning and recover signal from near-miss samples.
impact: Provides a practical recipe to stabilize reward signals and activate spatial reasoning in VLMs, enabling more reliable numeric 3D predictions for downstream tasks (robotics, scene reconstruction, AR) without heavy architecture changes.
visual_elements: Before vs after reward landscapes: sparse spikes (relative reward) contrasted with smooth continuous reward curves (SVR) showing denser gradients.
Flowchart of the pipeline: 3D scene → verifiable checks → SVR module → RL fine-tuning of VLM.
Illustration of near-miss examples: predicted vs ground-truth geometry with annotated small errors that are recovered by SVR.
Quantitative concept chart: training stability (gradient variance) and convergence illustration (schematic) comparing relative ranking vs SVR.
paper_title: Smooth Operator: Smooth Verifiable Reward Activates Spatial Reasoning Ability of Vision-Language Model
paper_authors: Siwen Jiao, Tianxiong Lv, Kangan Qian, Chenxu Zhao, Xiuyuan Zhu
